description:
## What

`src/fetcher/url_validator.cr` has 10+ IP-range-check methods with similar shapes:

- `link_local?` (IPv4 + IPv6 variants)
- `cgnat?`
- `benchmark?`
- `multicast?`
- `reserved?`
- `current_network?`
- `documentation?`
- `ipv6_unique?`
- `ipv6_site?`
- `ipv6_mapped_ipv4?`

Each does its own `ipv4_octets` parse, manual first/second octet checks, etc. Some use CIDR-style constants (`LINK_LOCAL_IPV4 = "169.254.0.0/16"`), some use per-octet constants.

## Why

DRY violation. 10+ methods with the same shape. Adding a new range to block (e.g., RFC 6890 unicast) requires a new method. Reading the code requires understanding each method's quirks.

## How

Replace the per-method logic with a data-driven table:

```crystal
BLOCKED_CIDR_RANGES = [
  IPAddress.parse("10.0.0.0/8"),
  IPAddress.parse("172.16.0.0/12"),
  IPAddress.parse("192.168.0.0/16"),
  IPAddress.parse("169.254.0.0/16"),
  # ...
]

private def self.blocked_ip?(ip) : Bool
  BLOCKED_CIDR_RANGES.any? { |range| range.includes?(ip) }
end
```

Crystal's `IPAddress` already provides `private?`, `loopback?`, and CIDR matching. The custom octet-parsing logic duplicates what IPAddress gives for free.

## Done when

- All 10+ per-method IP checks replaced by a single `blocked_ip?` that uses a CIDR table
- `spec/url_validator_spec.cr` still passes
- `spec/url_validator_ssrf_spec.cr` still passes
- `spec/security/url_sanitization_spec.cr` still passes
title: Refactor: deduplicate URLValidator IP-range checks via CIDR table
